**The culprit was ODock's running-apps list: its `RunningModel.qml` stores a live application object in the model row, and Qt segfaults converting that row after the object reference (`__entry`) becomes invalid. The only change made was turning that feature off — ODock's `showRunning` was set to `false` in `~/.config/omarchy/shell.json` — no plugin code was touched.**

- The session (codex 01a1d49f, started 2026-11-13, asked to diagnose a quickshell SIGSEGV PID 1982344 recorded by systemd-coredump) first found quickshell crashed on an invalid object pointer (`0xff00000200000000`) while converting model data for a QML item — codex 01a1d49f #38, #35.
- Decoding model data in three cores (Nov 11, 12 and 13) showed every crash on ODock's `__entry` field — the row ODock builds for running apps (`__entry`, `__running`, `appId`, `label`); RunningModel.qml:159 stores the live app object in the row and DockItem.qml:41 reads it back. ODock was installed Nov 2 at 10:51; the first saved matching crash followed at 11:32 — codex 01a1d49f #68, #63. At this point the agent had changed nothing ("I haven't changed any plugins or settings", #68).
- The user said "turn it off for now" (#69), and the agent edited `shell.json`, flipping ODock's `showRunning` from `true` to `false` while preserving the 10 pinned dock items and writing a backup `shell.json.before-odock-ejcd_ex7.bak` — codex 01a1d49f #73 (tool call), #74 (result: "ODock showRunning: false / Pinned items preserved: 10 / Backup: …"), confirmed on the live dock (#77). Dock.qml defaults `showRunning` to `true` (line 180) — #67. It deliberately did not patch the plugin; the suggested proper fix (store app IDs instead of live objects) was left as a recommendation (#68), and the icon-loading crashes' cause was left unresolved (#68).

What that session said already exists (`claude-code da3cef56 #58`):

- **A real code-editor element.** Herdr's copy of gpui-kit has `Editor` / `EditorState` — syntax highlighting by `language`, line numbers, folding, soft wrap, selection, undo through `replace()`, change events, and settable syntax colours; being GPUI it's the same framework family as Zed's editor. Verified by reading the shipped `.d.ts` (`claude-code da3cef56 #55`).
- **Safe file saving.** `writeTextFile(path, text, expected)` writes only if the file still matches what you loaded, replacing atomically — the same stale-snapshot protection Orca's editor API has (`claude-code da3cef56 #55`).
- **A shipped consumer, read-only.** The built-in Files mod already uses that editor: `~/.config/herdr-app/mods/files/main.js:141` builds it with `readonly: true` and never writes (`claude-code da3cef56 #57`).

Limits noted: `readTextFile` caps at 1 MiB, remote saving needs `exec(..., {on})`, no language server, and no web view so no Orca-style custom editors (`claude-code da3cef56 #58`). The finding was later recapped by the Orca-comparison follow-up (`claude-code 44f74336 #26`) and independently confirmed during the markdown-viewer side quest: Herdr deliberately ships the read-only code `Editor` as a building block and expects mods to assemble the rest (`claude-code 18496e3e #81`).

**Bounds on an API-kind run (src/ask.mjs):** a step limit and a wall-clock budget. `MAX_STEPS = 20` (src/ask.mjs:28) is the loop bound (`for (let step = 0; step < MAX_STEPS; step++)`, src/ask.mjs:382); a step is one model turn (answer or repl tool call). The clock is `timeoutSeconds` (tool schema: 30–900, default 300; src/ask.mjs:531,534) clamped to `max(20_000, min(timeoutSeconds*1000, clientMs ? clientMs - RESERVE_MS : Infinity))` (src/ask.mjs:539) — i.e. the client's `MCP_TOOL_TIMEOUT` minus the reserve if set.

**It warms once, then forks per question.** The instructions are loaded into a one-time `claude -p <prime>` session and every later question reuses that session as a fork — it never re-sends the instruction block.

**How the warm works**
- The warm call is `claude -p <D.prime> --append-system-prompt-file <INSTRUCTIONS>` (`src/ask.mjs:145`, args at `src/ask.mjs:125`); for the code domain the prime makes the model call `help` and run one `overview` cell, so the instructions, scripts and typed API all enter the session context (`domains/code/domain.mjs:34-36`).
- The resulting `session_id` plus the warm run's `total_cost_usd` is saved to `<STATE_DIR>/warm/claude-cli.json` (`src/ask.mjs:148-149`, file path at `src/ask.mjs:68` and `103`).
- Each question is a separate process: `claude -p <question + answerRules> --resume <warm.sessionId> --fork-session` (`src/ask.mjs:154,156`) — the fork inherits the warmed prefix, and forking keeps questions isolated. Follow-ups (`continue: true`) instead resume the previous fork's inner session (`src/ask.mjs:154`).
- Cost accounting mirrors this: the warm cost is stored (`src/ask.mjs:147-148`) and subtracted from each fork's reported total, so the journal shows only the question's real spend (`src/ask.mjs:158,168`). The only `cache_control` in the repo is on the separate `api` backend, not this one (`src/ask.mjs:350`).

**When it re-warms**
- Per question it computes a fingerprint: `sha([INSTRUCTIONS, ...ctx.fingerprintFiles()], JSON.stringify(BACKENDS[b]))` (`src/ask.mjs:72`, hash fn at `src/ask.mjs:33-42`). `fingerprintFiles()` is `src/server.mjs`, `src/core/toolkit.mjs`, the domain's `apiDoc` and `instructions`, the domain's own extra files, and every script `.mjs` (path + mtime) (`src/server.mjs:447-454`).
- The saved warm session is reused only when `s.fingerprint === fp && s.sessionId` (`src/ask.mjs:107`); any mismatch — editing instructions, scripts, API doc, server/toolkit code, or the backend's model config — means no warm hit and the prime runs again on the next question (`src/ask.mjs:141-149`), stated as the design in `README.md:102-105`.

- No time-based expiry: searched `warmTtl`, `warm_ttl`, `maxAge`, `expire`, `stale`, `resurrect` across `src/` — zero hits. Re-warming is purely fingerprint-driven; an untouched setup keeps its warm session indefinitely.
- No Anthropic prompt-caching (`cache_control`/`ephemeral`) markers on the claude-cli path — the reuse is session-level (resume + fork), not provider prompt caching; that mechanism belongs to the `api` backend only.
